meta.sourceSheet: worksheets 'island-tokens' and 'Island' of Isle-of-Farms-v42.xlsm (the token set and its seat scaling), plus 'map-cards' for the tile faces. The map-cards VP and crate columns are SUPERSEDED by the token island (16/09/2026).
notes: ⭐⭐⭐ 16/09/2026: THE TOKEN ISLAND (Dean, rulings R3 and R7; docs/vegetable-token-island-handoff-2026-09-16-v1.md §2). Every island card (tile) is seeded at setup with TWO TOKENS. A token is a DEMAND (2 cards of one crop, or a WILD token that takes any 2 cards, which may be different crops), a VP value (3, 4, 5 or 6) and, on the 3 and 4 VP tokens only (tokens.workerOnVp), a WORKER: the delivery meeple, drawn at random from the 25-meeple bag below. A delivery is ALWAYS tileRule.crates x tileRule.cardsPerCrate = 4 barn cards and there is no substitution. The FIRST delivery on a tile pays BOTH tokens' demands and then CHOOSES which token to take as its receipt (and that token's Worker). The SECOND delivery pays the remaining token's demand PLUS 2 cards of any crops (the printed '2 any' revealed under the taken token) and takes the last token; the tile is then finished. A receipt KEEPS ITS CROP (R7): a player's receipts are records of VP, crop ('wild' for a wild token) and tile. The end trigger is unchanged: six receipts.

THE TOKEN SET (worksheet island-tokens of Isle-of-Farms-v42.xlsm): for each crop in play one token at each of tokens.vpValues (6 / 5 / 4 / 3), plus tokens.wildBySeats wild tokens. The crops in play are the crops of the decks in play (decksInPlayBySeats, seats + 1), so 2 seats deal 3 crops x 4 = 12 tokens onto 6 tiles, 3 seats 4 x 4 + 2 wild = 18 onto 9, and 4 seats 5 x 4 + 4 wild = 24 onto 12. data.test.ts asserts that the pool exactly fills the tiles at every seat count.

⚠️ BUILDER DEFAULTS, NOT RULED BY DEAN (handoff §5 item 8): (1) when tokens.wildBySeats is below the number of VP values (3 seats: 2 of 4), WHICH wild values are used is drawn at random from tokens.vpValues with the game's seeded RNG; (2) the whole pool is shuffled and dealt two tokens per tile at random, so a tile MAY hold two tokens of the same crop (it then wants 4 cards of that crop on its first delivery); (3) Workers are dealt from the shuffled bag onto the worker-carrying tokens in deal order, so at 3 seats the Worker count varies with the wild values drawn (8 to 10).

THE WORKER IS THE DELIVERY MEEPLE OF 14/09/2026, MOVED ONTO THE TOKENS. Its spend rules are unchanged and live in rules.turn (meepleSpendTiming 'afterAction', meepleSpendPerTurn 1): after your main action you may discard one Worker for the PLAIN action of its colour, and it then leaves the game. The bag is 5 of each of the 5 colours, dealt from ALL FIVE colours whatever suits are at the table, because a Worker's action exists whether or not its suit is farmed. tokens.workerOnVp [] seeds no Worker at all, which is how an overlay reproduces the game without the delivery meeple. poolSize is stored rather than derived so that an overlay moving perColour has to move it too, and data.test.ts asserts the two agree. faceUpAtSetup is recorded and read by nothing.

⛔ DELETED 16/09/2026 WITH THE TOKEN ISLAND: vpByDeliveryOrder (the flat island's 6 / 3 VP by fill order, 09/08/2026), demandTokensBySeats (one demand token per crate, perSuit 4 plus cornucopias), meeples.perDeliverySpace and meeples.seededSpaces (which delivery SPACES carried a meeple), and with them rules.turn.deliverySpaceChoice and rules.turn.deliveryMeepleSpace. There are no delivery spaces any more: a tile holds tokens, a token is taken whole, and its VP is printed on the token rather than decided by arrival order. V6's face-down demand token (the Vegetable rebuild of 09/08/2026) was deleted in the same pass because v42's V6 prints something else. V5's SWAP survives as a token swap between two different tiles, each token keeping its VP and its Worker.

tileRule: crates is the number of tokens dealt onto a tile (2) and cardsPerCrate the cards one token's demand asks for (2), so their product is the 4-card delivery. coinsPerDelivery IS A TOMBSTONE, PINNED AT 0 since v31 deleted coins; nothing reads it and it has no knob.

The END TRIGGER lives in rules.json (endGame.trigger = deliveryCount, deliveriesToTrigger = 6): one seat's sixth receipt ends the game. V14's 'take every receipt on the island card' counts both tokens it takes.

LEVEL IS ART. tiles[].level and slotsBySeats survive because the physical island is still built as a pyramid out of the printed map cards, and the bookend rule below decides which faces are on the table. Nothing mechanical reads a level. slotsBySeats follows seats+1 / seats / seats-1 by level, giving 6 / 9 / 12 tiles. The pyramid is cosmetic in the strong sense: adjacency is null by decision, and any tile with a token left is a legal delivery target on any turn.
seats counts players at the table. There is no one-seat board: a solo game is a two-seat game in which a bot occupies the second seat.

Exactly (seats + 1) suit decks are in play: one owned by each seat, plus one passive suit nobody farms but everybody may draw from and the island demands. The remaining suits are out of the game entirely, which is why the token pool spans exactly the crops of the decks on the table.

Bookend rule: the art paints each row's first printed face (A1 / B1 / C1) as the island's left edge and its last (A5 / B4 / C3) as the right edge, so a row with n tiles in play uses the first (n - 1) printed faces plus the row-end face. The 3-tile level-1 row is therefore A1, A2, A5.
At 2 seats the lone level-3 tile is D1 rather than C1. D1 prints no mechanical difference from C1; it is a distinct illustration for the two-player board.
unresolved: THE TOKEN SETUP DEFAULTS (handoff §5 item 8): which 2 of the 4 wild tokens a 3-seat game uses, and whether one island card may hold two tokens of the same crop. Both are builder defaults (random) until Dean rules.

WHETHER A PLAYER EVER GIVES UP VP FOR A WORKER. The bots priced the old 3 VP space plus meeple below 6 VP and never took it (0.0% on reference-v19). The token set narrows the gap to 1 VP (a 4 VP token with a Worker against a 5 VP token without), so the token choice is the reading to watch.
D1 and C1 print identical faces, so the two-seat substitution is purely illustrative. Confirm that is what is wanted, or drop D1 and let 2p use C3.
The six-receipt end trigger is not scaled by seat count. If the 2-player game runs long at the table, the dial is either the trigger (a per-seat row) or slotsBySeats.
